caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 2505 of 2013
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Naser Uddin Chowdhury, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners. 
Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No 1. Respondent Nos. 2-3 Not represented.
parties:
Most. Amena Khatun and others
Vs.
Shuja Nagar Shashan Committee, represented by its secretary Sri Kumaresh Kumar Odhikari and others
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J: This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.06.2013 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3583 of 2005 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No 13 of 1984 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna, for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession of the Suit property measuring .20 acre of land under plot No. 633 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 4, S.A. Khatian No. 275 of Mouja Sufanagar, stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to ex-landlord Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and others and they possessed the same as it was under their khas possession. Being approached by the Hindu Community for using the suit property as cremation ground, the ex-landlords approved their proposal and consequently allowed them to create a cremation ground thereon and, thereafter, the suit property has been used as cremation ground by the local Hindu Community and for the aforesaid reason an Ekrarnama dated 22.03.1947 was executed by the ex-landlords in respect of the suit property and its possession was delivered to the plaintiff committee and since then the plaintiff committee has been using the suit property as cremation ground for more than 12 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants. The ex-landlords never settled the suit property to anybody. The cremations on file suit property has been managed by the local Hindu Community through a committee and the plaintiff being Secretary of the committee instituted the above suit. S.A. record was wrongly prepared in the name of defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 1 being purchaser from defendant No. 2 claimed his title over the suit property in the month of Baishakh, 1983 and denied the title of the plaintiff. The plaintiff was not aware of the wrong S.A. record and deed of purchase of defendant No. 1. During S.A. survey, the Survey Officer told the plaintiff that the suit land would be recorded as Government khan land showing possession of the Committee with remarks for public use. Subsequently, defendant No. 3 son of defendant No. 1 in the year 1982 dispossessed the plaintiff and an allegation was filed before the S.D.O. Sadar, Pabna. Hence, the plaintiff Committee represented by its Secretary filed the suit.

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury, Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and Tarak Gobinda Chowdhury. Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury settled the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh (defendant No.2), who on settlement got possession of the same on payment of rents to the ex-landlord. During S.A. operation, the suit property was recorded in the mime of the, ex-landlord Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury and Dukhu Sheikh filed Objection Case No. 26 of 1960 and got S.A. record in his name and, thereafter, Dukhu Sheikh transferred the suit property by registered deed dated 03.10.1962 in favour of defendant No. 1 and delivered possession in his favour. Defendant No. 1 mutated the suit property in his name and paid rent to the government. The plaintiff never acquired any title and possession to the suit land. During liberation war the patni papers of Dukhu Sheikh were lost and thus those could not be delivered in favour of defendant No. 1.

4. Defendant No. 3 appeared and filed additional written statement and denied the claim of the plaintiff that he dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property on behalf of the defendant No. 1 and that the plaintiff filed an allegation to the local S.D.O. to that effect.

5. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna by his judgment and decree dated 11.04.2002 decreed the suit.

6. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the trial Court the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 93 of 2002 and upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record the learned Special District Judge, Pabna allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the appellate Court the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 3583 of 2005 before the High Court Division, and obtained Rule. By the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Hence, the defendants as petitioners have tiled the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

8. Mr. Md. Naser Uddin Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that Dukhu Sheikh defendant No. 2, the vendor of the predecessor of the defendants-petitioners, got the land from the jaminder Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury by way of settlement and accordingly S.A. Khatian was prepared in his name. Thereafter, defendant No. 2 sold the suit land to defendant No. 1, who mutated the land in his name and paid all taxes to the Government. The present petitioners are in possession of the suit land and are using part of it as their homestead. He submitted that the evidence of the Advocate Commissioner shows that the land was never used as a cremation ground and the ekrarnama of the Jaminder for this purpose was not acted upon and for that reason the land was returned to the original landlord, who then settled the suit land in favour of defendant No. 2 Dukhu Sheikh. He submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that the plaintiff was unable to prove his right title, possession and dispossession of the suit land by producing legally acceptable documentary and oral evidence. He finally submitted that Dukhu Sheikh, having sold the land in 1962, lost his title and possession and, hence the solenama, nadabinama and deposition of Dukhu Sheikh in Court are of no value.

9. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondents made submission in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and other connected papers on record.

<u>11. A perusal of the judgment of the appellate Court discloses that the evidence of the witnesses was not discussed whereas the trial Court observed that P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 consistently deposed that the suit land has been used as cremation ground. The trial Court further observed that defendant No. 2, who deposed as P.W.1, filed a solenama stating inter alia, that the suit land was never settled in his favour and that he did not execute any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 on 03.10.1962, but defendant No. 1 did not cross-examine hint to controvert his statement and deposition. The lower appellate Court, on the other hand, reversed the decree of the trial Court, upon relying on the deed of sale, executed by defendant No. 2 in the year 1962 and the consequent record of rights in favour of defendant No. 1. The appellate Court also relied upon the fact that the plaintiff committee neither took any step to record its name in the S.A. record nor paid any tax in respect of the suit land, nor produced any papers in respect of the use of the land as a cremation ground and thereby allowed the appeal.</u>

12. The High Court Division discussed the evidence of the witnesses and observed that among the P.Ws, P.W. 5 is a member of the Muslim community, who deposed corroborating the plaintiffs claim that the property was used as cremation ground. The High Court Division noted that D.W.4, the Deed Writer, deposed in support of the registration of the deed of 1962, but since the executant (defendant No. 2) did not admit the execution of the deed, the evidence of D.W. 4 did not help the defendants. The High Court Division also observed that there were no papers produced in support of the alleged settlement of the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh (defendant No. 2). The High Court Division concluded that mere mutation and payment of rent does not confer title to the defendants.

13. The defendants did not produce any evidence with regard to the alleged settlement of the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh by the Jamindar giving an explanation that the papers were lost during the liberation war. In the absence of such papers and in view of the positive evidence of defendant No. 2 Dukhu Sheikh that he did not get settlement of the suit property from the Jamindar, nor executed any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 in 1962, the High Court Division rightly excluded the evidence of D.W. 4; the Deed Writer. Moreover, the High Court Division observed that D.W. I himself, although alive at the time of trial and present in the Court did not depose in support of the defendants' case. The son of defendant No. 1, who deposed in Court merely stated that his father (defendant No. 1) was present in the Court, but unwell. However he did not produce any medical certificate in support. In this regard the High Court Division accepted the claim of the plaintiff that D. W. 1 did not depose because he would not wish to depose falsely. In our view the High Court Division correctly concluded that since the settlement in favour of Dukhu Sheikh does not stand, the S.A. record in his favour has no basis.

14. We find that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and does not call for any interference. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.
